requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: The persistent pwquality policy sets minlen=12, pam_pwquality is active in the common password stack, and both before and after restart an 11-character password was rejected while a compliant 12-character password passed.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must contain at least three different character classes.
requirements.summary: The persistent policy sets minclass=3, and functional checks rejected a 12-character password containing only two classes while accepting one containing four classes, including after restart.

overall_summary: Both password-complexity outcomes are satisfied. The restart protocol is coherent: node1 was healthy before restart, the reboot was acknowledged, its boot identity changed from 3fad4432-1dea-40c8-b4f1-970d19eb5f34 to 13c7695e-e317-4861-a54f-5775e2286e9d, and the running system retained its PAM integration, policy, and functional behavior afterward. Fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot transition and healthy final state.
limitations: Functional enforcement was tested with pwscore against the configured pwquality policy rather than through an end-to-end password-changing transaction. The observed PAM stack strongly supports application to new user passwords, but the complete interactive path was not directly exercised.
The topology has no separate application service, task data store, or multi-node cluster state to validate during restart recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation supplied the required PAM module and verification utility; the policy-file change implemented the task; testing was bounded; and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. Temporary test-output files created by cmd-0d90f1b3918d49be were absent from the final /tmp inventory. Final observations show healthy package state, no failed services, and no unsafe new listening service.
